Two articles released under the cap; five held back for a missing focus

Focus routing released 2 articles and held 5. The held stories were targeted at Discovery, Health & How Science Works, Agriculture & Ranching, and Digital Life & Security, and none of those focuses was active tonight. The two releases were both climate-and-disaster stories that landed in the current theme, and they were held since 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-26 respectively. Five stories waited for focus windows that did not arrive in this run.

The roundup opened on local news, but 42 stories were cut for airtime

The roundup pool kept 18 stories (10 theme, 8 local), and 42 were dropped by the airtime budget under NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT. Of 9 local stories available, 8 aired, and the roundup opened on local news. The cut is by design: the pool is larger than one segment can carry, and a dropped story can resurface on a better-matched day. The thing to watch is the imbalance in the cut itself. 18 unused on-theme candidates were left behind, which is the reserve the next runs draw from.

The short first draft was expanded, and the shipped script still fell short of its target

The first draft came in at 2768 words against a target of 3400, so it went back for one expand pass. The shipped script is 3669 words, above target. That is the number that counts; the first-draft shortfall was corrected before release. Shipping at 3669 words means the expand pass did its job, and the episode met length without padding past the target.

One TTS take came back short and stayed short after retry

One TTS segment returned shorter than its word count predicted and was retried once. The retry was still short, so the longer of the two takes was kept. Nothing was dropped from the episode. The single occurrence is the only audio irregularity in the run.

Script vs. storyboard: loosely kept. The episode keeps the plan's central question, stances and landing, but the deep dive adds a long Indonesia fire-weather and palm oil digression and drops the Chilcotin-specific claim about the nation's and community forest's governance. The roundup mostly holds its order, with the Quesnel airport and Legion stories tightened and the Burwell family story moved and reshaped.

items.content_html:
Theme: Indigenous Lands & Innovation. Focus: Economic Development (week 3 of 4). Run 45780240933.

▲
Shipped, needs a look2 things to look at before tomorrow's run.

What to do

  1. script/debate-summary fell back. Search the run log for Degraded 'script/debate-summary' and decide whether the fallback is acceptable or the cause needs fixing.
    degrade() row: Claude debate extraction failed, used keyword fallback: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 2940 (char 2939)
  2. Investigate.
    one subject aired in separate places: public service

What happened

Focus rotation fell back to the base theme because no article matched

The scheduled focus for this cycle was Economic Development (week 3 of 4), but zero articles matched it. The pipeline logged the fallback and used the base theme selection, Indigenous Lands & Innovation, instead. Of the 67 articles loaded, 20 were theme articles and 41 were bonus articles. The fallback meant the day's focus segment was built from the general theme pool rather than from economic-development material.

Focus routing still ran in parallel. One held article was released ([APTN News] AFN calls for strengthening of First Nations Cle..., held since 2026-11-25), and three remain held: a Recreation & Backcountry Access piece dated 2026-11-27, a Digital Life & Security piece dated 2026-12-02, and an Agriculture & Ranching piece dated 2026-12-08. Those three will wait for their own focus days. If Economic Development stays thin across the cycle, the focus rotation should be reviewed against the feed mix; the intake pool needs more economic coverage before the next Economic Development week.

Debate extraction failed and fell back to keyword matching

Claude's debate-summary extraction failed with an unterminated string at line 1, column 2940, and a batch debate-summary parse failed separately at column 2916. Both were JSON truncation errors, which suggests the model output was cut off before the closing bracket. The pipeline fell back to keyword extraction for the debate summary. The listener gets a debate question, Deep dive on Indigenous Lands & Innovation, that was pulled by keyword rather than by reading the segment, so it may describe the topic less precisely than the model would have. The script itself passed quality checks: 0 AI-tell pattern hits, and a Casey-to-Riley voice ratio of 0.79.

Both warnings point at the same output-length limit. Raising the token budget for the debate-extraction call, or adding a retry that requests a shorter summary on parse failure, should be the first change to test.

Script came in under target and shipped under target

The first draft came in at 2958 words against a target of 3400. The pipeline sent it back for one expand pass, and the shipped script was 3565 words, which is above target. The expand pass was enough to clear the target, so the thin first draft did not reach the listener. Only one expand pass is allowed per run, so a first draft that starts much thinner would not have been rescued the same way.

Roundup citations matched 12 of 18, and deep-dive citations matched 4 of 4. The roundup gap is the more useful number: 6 roundup citations did not match a source, and that is where a listener checking the references would find something missing. The roundup pool held 18 stories and dropped 24 to the airtime budget by design, so the 18 that aired were the ones the pipeline ranked highest, not a shortfall. The citation mismatch should be looked at before the next run that carries a similar roundup load.

Script vs. storyboard: loosely kept. The episode mostly follows the plan's shape, but the roundup frame is replaced by a different opening, several roundup stories are dropped or merged, and the deep dive drops the Kalshi and C-39 pushback framing and adds a new contested detail about Seabridge and the Tsetsaut case. The landing is left open as planned, but the Cariboo beat is substantially reworked.

The cycle was in week 2 of 5 on the focus Homestead & Off-Grid Tech, but zero articles matched it. The pipeline needs at least 4, so it fell back to the base theme selection, Gear, Gadgets & Practical Tech, with the theme feed Repair Culture & Practical Tech. Of 78 articles loaded, 19 were on theme and 58 were bonus. After 65 were removed as duplicates, 3 were released by focus routing and 7 were held for other focus days. The listener got the standing theme for the day, not the week's planned focus, and nothing on the homestead theme aired.

The held queue shows what the routing sent to other days. Seven items were held, four of them for Discovery, Health & How Science Works and Economic Development, and the earliest release date is 2026-11-26. Nothing was lost, but the focus cycle will not carry the homestead story unless homestead articles arrive on their own.

Change: if zero-match weeks recur, check the homestead feed sources in the focus configuration before the cycle starts, not after it has already fallen back.

Roundup built from 18 stories; 39 cut by the airtime budget

The roundup pool held 18 stories, 13 on theme and 5 local. All 5 local stories aired, and the roundup opened on local news. The airtime budget cut 39 stories from the pool; by design those can resurface on a better-matched day. The short-script result is the tension to watch: the first draft came in at 2738 words against a target of 3400, was sent back for one expand pass, and shipped at 3255 words. That is under target but above the short-episode threshold, so no alert fired.

Citations were matched on 14 of 18 roundup stories and 2 of 4 deep-dive stories, so the deep dive is the weaker of the two on sourcing.

Change: none for the budget. If the citation gap on deep dives repeats, inspect the four deep-dive source links in the script stage.

Weather came from Environment Canada; Open-Meteo did not respond

Open-Meteo did not answer, so the weather segment used the Environment Canada forecast. Williams Lake was reported, and Horsefly got no figure. Listeners in Horsefly heard no forecast for their own town.

Change: add a Horsefly fallback source to the weather step, or drop the town from the segment when the primary feed is down.

One TTS take stayed short after retry; the longer take was kept

One TTS take came back shorter than its word count predicted and was retried. The retry was still short, so the longer of the two takes was kept and nothing was dropped from the episode. The retry count is one take, not a run of problems.
